description: 1) apps/gateway/src/vendors/api.rs import_models derived model alias prefixes from vendor.name (the API-key connection label, e.g. 'Primary inference' or 'qiniu-personal-qualification') instead of the owning Provider business slug (e.g. 'qiniu'), causing imported models under a Provider to inherit the API key's label as their namespace prefix. Full root-cause diagnosis completed: (1) On staging, codex-staging-ux created a synthetic personal connection named 'qiniu-personal-qualification' (create_supplier=true + personal_organization_id) on 2026-11-07 for niu-cvz to bypass commercial qualification/pricing AND global vendor_models.alias PK collision with qiniu/*, and never cleaned it up; (2) import_models (apps/gateway/src/vendors/api.rs:2897) derives model prefix from vendor.name (API key label) instead of owning Provider slug, while vendor_models.alias shares a single global PK across commercial and personal_vendor_ownership routes, and Resale API still accepts personal_organization_id despite zero UI support; (3) routes.rs:3110 returns generation_capabilities.chat=null whenever OpenAI-compatible /v1/models lacks OpenRouter-only output_modalities (unless Qiniu HTML scraper matched), and ModelTable.tsx layered two conflicting historical workarounds (niu-lxs.17 Open Generations vs niu-cvz Try in Chat) that point to the exact same URL.
title: Use owning Provider slug for imported model aliases and simplify model trial CTA to 'Try' (试用)

acceptance_criteria: For supported UI languages, missing and invalid login fields present a localized, understandable error associated with the field and announced to assistive technology; keyboard users can correct and resubmit. Verify Chinese and English with a browser whose own language differs, and test both password and access-token modes without exposing credentials.
close_reason: Login now validates missing/invalid fields in the selected UI language with noValidate and an associated role=alert error; under an en-US browser locale the Chinese UI rendered 请输入邮箱地址。 instead of the native English message. Login suites 18/18, i18n 0 findings, typecheck passes.
description: On 2026-11-03 in the in-app browser, staging /login in Simplified Chinese displayed the browser-native English message “Please fill out this field.” after submitting the empty email/password form. Focus correctly moved to email, but users selecting Chinese must interpret an English error at the first step. Native validation language depends on the browser and this observation does not establish all browser locales or other fields. Deployed revision was not independently identified. See docs/ux/staging-review-2026-11-02.md, story S02.
notes:
The empty access-token form was also checked in the same Chinese in-app browser session: focus moved to the token field and the same English native required-field prompt appeared. No credential was entered.
Entering a synthetic email without @ and submitting also produced an English native email-format message in the Chinese interface; no password was entered and native validation prevented form submission.
title: Localize login form validation to the selected interface language

acceptance_criteria: Reproduce with the affected client and capture the failing request or local operation and error category without secrets. If the message is product-owned, show the user the affected operation, a truthful actionable recovery, and a safe diagnostic reference; cover permission, network and service errors without claiming an unverified cause. Reconcile with any matching existing issue before implementation.
close_reason: Rejected: user confirmed the reported error is not a Niu issue.
description: On 2026-11-03 the user reported seeing “workspace routing discovery failed” and asked what it means. The page or client, complete error, triggering action and deployed revision were not provided. A literal search of the local Niu source and a filtered staging Render log query found no matching message; that does not establish the failure cause or source. The phrase alone does not give a user a cause or recovery step. Obtain context and reproduce before attributing a root cause or prescribing a fix. See docs/ux/staging-review-2026-11-02.md.
title: Investigate reported workspace routing discovery failure and its recovery message

acceptance_criteria: Clearly identify self-revocation and its consequences before confirmation. When authoritative membership establishes this is the final owner, prevent removal and explain how to transfer ownership; enforce the invariant server-side. Test other owners, scoped members, stale/concurrent membership, and authorized denial without removing real access.
close_reason: Self-revocation dialog now states this is your current account, revoking ends all your sessions immediately, and the server blocks removing the last owner; it instructs transferring ownership first. Browser verified on real Second Studio organization members page with one Demo owner; action dialog shows both warnings before the destructive confirm. Implementation is in handoff commit f9855adf.
description: On 2026-11-03 staging organization settings > Members listed one visible active owner, which matched the signed-in account. Its Actions menu offered Revoke access, and the confirmation stated that organization-wide access to every workspace would be removed, with an enabled Revoke access button. It did not identify this as the current account or explain last-owner protection. Cancel was used; no revocation was submitted, and the complete membership or server enforcement was not verified. This is a decision-support finding, not a claim that backend permits removing the final owner. See S13 and docs/ux/staging-review-2026-11-02.md.
notes: Reopened 2026-11-06 after UI closure audit: close evidence did not cover the full rendered/acceptance state (representative data, desktop+narrow, error/return paths, or deployed artifact). Code may be present in f9855adf/1bc321fb; status stays open until browser evidence matches AC.
title: Clarify self-revocation and last-owner protection before confirming access removal

Inspect a mature reference and preserve Niu tokens and existing component rules.
close_reason: Phone layout now keeps a 54px product rail at the left of the floating sidebar instead of hiding it. At 390px the rail is 54px, sheet starts at 54px (256px wide), main content starts at 54px (336px), toggle is at x=70 and there is no horizontal overflow; 320px also fits at 54/256/266. The sheet account entry shows avatar+Demo and opens account/organization/settings/sign-out actions; rail links navigate (Models verified, sheet closes). Escape now closes the sheet and returns focus to the toggle. Sidebar/account/admin tests 22/22, typecheck and dashboard build pass.
description: User-provided staging screenshot on 2026-11-03 shows a prominent Navigation button in the floating sidebar, where the user expected their name and account information. User direction: place the product rail at the left side of the floating sidebar, and use a recognizable account identity entry instead of labeling that entry Navigation. Local AccountMenu.tsx combines product navigation and account actions under a mobile Navigation trigger; local source is not proof of the deployed revision. The attempted 390px in-app browser override did not take effect in the new tab, so independently reproduce on an actual narrow viewport before implementation. Reproduced in the signed-in Chinese in-app browser at 390 × 844 on 2026-11-03: collapsed workspace view hides the product rail; expanding the sidebar shows workspace sections and a bottom Navigation trigger. That menu combines product destinations with the signed-in identity, role, current organization and account actions. The user identity is therefore revealed only after opening a control named Navigation. Actual touch hardware and other roles remain unverified.

User clarification 2026-11-03: the product rail should sit on the left side of the floating sidebar. Preserve this spatial relationship whenever that sidebar is floating; do not interpret the direction as limited to a particular viewport. Verify the actual available layouts before design or implementation.

2026-11-05 prototype 2 at 390px: showing the 54px rail plus the 54px spacer moves the sidebar toggle to x=70 and keeps main content at x=54 (336px wide, no horizontal overflow). The portalled sheet still needs its open-state left/transform corrected (measured x=-162 during the open transition), and the rail account trigger shows only the avatar initial. Not shipped.
title: Unify mobile product rail and sidebar; show account identity in its menu trigger

description:
Style audit follow-up (release/0.4 c6ec138a, 1440/1024/768/390 browser measurements).

Findings:
1. Page gutters and page-header inline padding are declared in foundation.css, shell.css, operations.css and surfaces.css with conflicting/dead media rules. At 769-959px tabbed headers place the 56px tab strip inside a 40px padded header content box (tab triggers overflow the header top/bottom), and tabs start after the mobile navigation toggle (x=70) while content starts at x=24, violating the 'tabs flush with .page-content gutter' invariant.
2. Header tab height/order changes are split across max-width 768 and shell 959/580 blocks; only some properties win, so triggers remain 56px while the slot/list is 40px.
3. Dialog framing is re-declared per call site (max-h 85dvh/90dvh/90vh, some omitted); DialogContent has no default bounded scroll, the close control is a ~16px target, and DialogHeader does not reserve space for it, so long titles can underlap the close button.
4. BillingView chooses whether to render a second local tab strip by reading document during render and hides it when #dashboard-page-tabs exists; ShellSectionTabs/PageHeader also read document during render for portal targets, creating SSR/client divergence and a local duplicate-tab workaround.
5. Page-content horizontal gutters currently: 32/24/16, but header gutters at 768 are 16 while content is 24 (accidental alignment) and at 769-959 tabs are offset by the mobile toggle.

Acceptance:
- Single --page-gutter source (32/24/16) drives .page-content and .dashboard-page-header; tabbed headers wrap to their own full-width 40px row at <=959 with tabs flush to content at 1440/1024/900/768/700/390.
- No tab trigger exceeds its slot/header at any width; no horizontal overflow.
- DialogContent has a default bounded scroll frame; DialogHeader reserves close-button space; close target >=24px; local max-h/flex overrides still win.
- No document reads during render for PageHeader/ShellSectionTabs portal targets; Billing renders exactly one tab strip.
- Regression tests cover gutter/header CSS, dialog defaults, and no local billing tab strip.
- Browser verified light/dark and en/zh-CN at 1440, 1024, 768, 390.
notes:
Implemented in 77a61518.

Changed:
- One --page-gutter token (32/24/16) shared by .page-content and .dashboard-page-header; removed conflicting/dead page-content padding rules from foundation.css and inline header padding from shell/surfaces media blocks.
- Tabbed headers wrap onto their own full-width 40px row at <=959px, with tabs flush to the content gutter; header tab height no longer overflows the padded 56px header row.
- PageHeader/ShellSectionTabs resolve portal hosts in useLayoutEffect with an SSR-safe inline fallback; BillingView no longer reads document during render or duplicates the shell tab strip.
- DialogContent owns max-h-[90dvh] overflow-y-auto overscroll-contain; DialogHeader reserves the close-control gutter; DialogTitle uses leading-snug; the shared close target is 32x32 with a hover/focus treatment. Swept 66 redundant per-dialog max-h/overflow declarations.
- Removed the last CJK-unsafe leading-none chart labels.
- Added regression tests for gutters, header wrapping, portal hydration, single billing tabs, dialog defaults, and duplicate dialog-frame classes. Updated AGENTS.md and docs/ux/ui-consistency-standard.md.

- Isolated worktree built from the committed tree: pnpm build:dashboard passed (includes i18n check, typegen, tsc, Vite build); tsc standalone passed.
- Browser (light/dark, en/zh-CN): measured header tabs flush to page content at 1440/1024/959/900/768/700/580/390; tab triggers fit within the header at every width; no horizontal document overflow.
- Guardrails dialogs at 390: bounded frame, 32px close target, 36px header close gutter, title leading 1.375; PolicyEditor inner-scroll override preserved.
- Billing: exactly one top tab strip, zero local tab strips.
- Console: no hydration/error events captured during dialog and route checks.

- Vitest cannot start this suite in the current Node 22.23 + Vite 8 environment: importing node:fs/node:path is externalized (No such built-in module: node:). Reproduced on untouched HEAD before this patch, so it is not caused by the change. The regression assertions were also executed directly with node and passed; CI Node 20 remains the authoritative test run.

description: At HEAD 282dd68, migration_compatibility::run reads legacy receipts before acquiring a migration lock, releases the SQLx lock after legacy steps, and collapses migration receipts in a separate unguarded transaction. description: Trigger: apps/gateway/src/request_payloads.rs:132 defaults payload capture to true; capture() buffers up to 1 MiB of request bytes (142-190) and tees the response stream into another 1 MiB buffer, then writes to storage through a global semaphore of 4 (request_payloads.rs:15). request_timings.rs:104-150 writes a timing row per attempt through another semaphore of 4. Impact: extra copies, memory held for slow streams and a fixed write-concurrency ceiling on the hot path; payload retention is a privacy/data-minimization decision made per request by default. Limits: no write saturation measured; storage retention is documented as 24h.

close_reason: Measured before/after on same Apple M4/PG17.11: hot-path statements/request 35.076 -> 30.041 (-5.035); p50/p95 6.642/14.072 ms -> 3.229/6.917 ms (50 warmups + 800 requests x3; shared host loaded, statement counts controlled). Readiness 3 statements -> 1 via payment_readiness_facts; no TTL readiness cache (expiring evidence has no monotonic revision, avoids stale positive); immutable currency singleton cached positive-only; migration 0425 materializes verified callback digests for O(1) readiness; removed 3 per-request set_config RTs (BEGIN+SET LOCAL one message) and REPEATABLE READ from single-statement key-policy reads. Remaining pre-dispatch budget: 3 authoritative reads + registry; durable writes dominate 30 statements. Benchmark script/docs recorded; cargo check, gateway 175, storage lib 41, PG readiness/callback/snapshot/key-policy tests, OpenAPI/migration/audience checks pass. Caveat: before/after binaries came from a shared dirty tree (unrelated invitation/media changes), hashes recorded.

description:
Trigger: Connect a Provider in /admin/providers (or create a duplicate/test Provider connection) and attempt to delete or disconnect it.
Impact: There is no DELETE /api/v1/vendors/:id endpoint and no Delete/Disconnect button anywhere in /admin/providers. Even at the PostgreSQL schema level, deleting a row from vendors fails with 'violates foreign key constraint vendor_audit_events_vendor_id_fkey' while vendor_audit_events has a BEFORE DELETE trigger (reject_accounting_mutation) that forbids deletion. Once created, a Provider connection can never be removed.
Source: apps/gateway/src/vendors/api.rs, crates/storage/migrations/0001_initial_schema.sql, apps/dashboard/app/features/providers/ProvidersView.tsx.
Acceptance criteria:
- Allow administrators to delete/disconnect a Provider connection cleanly from the UI and API while preserving audit integrity.
notes: 2026-11-04 source revalidation: ProviderEditor exposes an enabled-for-inference toggle and confirmation; disabling stops new requests but explicitly preserves the key for audit and permits re-enabling. This is not equivalent to removing or retiring an unwanted connection or erasing its credential. Hard-deleting immutable audit rows is not an acceptable remedy. Confirm actual runtime behavior and choose an auditable lifecycle before implementation.
title: Provide an auditable Provider connection retirement path

acceptance_criteria: 1. Allow toggling platform-configured external detectors directly with inline metadata without a modal legal-consent ceremony or brittle SHA-256 fingerprint request lockouts.
close_reason: Rejected as contrary to the documented required-input detector privacy design. docs/releases/required-input-detector-verification.md requires explicit external-processing consent, a versioned processing fingerprint and fresh review when detector configuration changes; activation/preview/assignment reject absent consent, unknown cost and stale fingerprints. Removing the consent checkbox and fingerprint lockout would allow silent external text processing across configuration revisions and contradicts the security contract. Current UI correctly has no detector service configured and performs no external processing. UX simplification should preserve consent/fingerprint semantics rather than delete them.
description:
Trigger: Enabling an external detector in '/workspaces/:ws/guardrails/detectors' or when an admin updates detector configuration.
Impact: ExternalDetectors.tsx:59-98 and DetectorPreview.tsx:57-73 force the workspace developer through a modal legal-consent ceremony ('I approve sending this workspace’s request text to this recipient under these declared conditions.') that binds a 64-char SHA-256 'configuration_fingerprint'. Any platform admin update to the detector's timeout or metadata invalidates the fingerprint and blocks all workspace inference requests ('Review required · requests remain blocked', line 77).
Source: apps/dashboard/app/features/guardrails/ExternalDetectors.tsx:59-98; apps/dashboard/app/features/guardrails/DetectorPreview.tsx:57-73.
notes: 2026-11-05 triage: removing external-detector consent/SHA binding changes a privacy/legal control; needs explicit security/privacy sign-off and a replacement authorization model before code changes.
title: Remove External Detector legal consent modal and SHA-256 configuration_fingerprint lockout in Guardrails

close_reason: Qiniu account_chat_banned is no longer swallowed: catalog import (vendors/api.rs:1771) and inference rejection mapping (web/inference/common.rs:66) detect the exact Qiniu base + HTTP 403 + account_chat_banned body and return the specific message 'The Qiniu account is not permitted to use chat services (account_chat_banned). Contact Qiniu to restore account access.' The classifier requires exact provider/status/code and the unit test verifies it, while the message contains no private secret. General upstream 4xx/5xx still use bounded generic messages, as intended.
description:
Trigger: Connect Qiniu or send a chat completion request using a Qiniu API key whose account returns HTTP 403 {"error":{"message":"Account is not permitted to use chat services","type":"access_denied_error","code":"account_chat_banned"}}. Also note that GET https://api.qnaigc.com/v1/models returns 200 OK without Authorization but 403 account_chat_banned when Authorization is sent for a chat-restricted key.
Impact: During catalog import (/api/v1/vendors/:id/catalog and /import), Niu discards the upstream error message/code and shows 'The provider rejected the saved API key. Check the key and provider account access.' During chat inference in /generations, Niu shows 'The provider refused this request. Check credential access and regional model availability'. The user never sees the actual upstream error reason ('Account is not permitted to use chat services' / account_chat_banned).
Source: apps/gateway/src/vendors/api.rs:1743-1762, apps/gateway/src/web/inference/.
Acceptance criteria:
- Surface sanitized upstream error messages and error codes (e.g. account_chat_banned: Account is not permitted to use chat services) in catalog discovery, connection check, and inference failure responses.
notes: 2026-11-04: For the canonical Qiniu endpoint and exact HTTP 403 account_chat_banned code, bounded error parsing now returns a fixed account-access remedy in catalog discovery/import and buffered/streaming Chat, preserving inference status and failure attribution without forwarding arbitrary upstream text. Model connection checks return a distinct status; API docs/contracts and SDK types were regenerated, and Chinese UI translation added. Rust classification and HTTP rejection tests, 78 connect/Chat tests, 4 model-check UI tests, dashboard type check, i18n and API contract check passed. Other upstream reasons and inference protocols still use safe generic errors. Real Qiniu account is disabled and UI behavior on the deployed revision, live connection checks, limits, malicious/large error bodies and narrow layouts need further end-to-end verification. Repository-wide cargo fmt check also reports unrelated existing formatting in admin.rs and api_migrations.rs.
title: UX/E2E: Upstream Provider error messages (e.g. Qiniu account_chat_banned) are swallowed during catalog import and inference

An existing key's Limits section reports unresolved requests and unknown committed token usage with unbounded requests. It offers limit History/Edit but no link to the exact affected requests or explanation there of the resulting capacity implications. Proposed direction: explain whether uncertainty affects admission and link the exact affected records to supported diagnosis/reconciliation. If no safe reconciliation exists, name the responsible operational procedure; do not offer unconditional release or automatic resubmission.

Source: docs/ux/findings.md (UX-11). Latest reconciliation: docs/ux/continuation-2026-10-21.md, All findings reconciled.

Imported disposition: Partly corrected: catalog uses Default; Playground Popular still falls back to first usable models

Recheck current code/rendering before implementing; migration is not a new reproduction or authorization for product changes.

**P2 · decision semantics · G3–G4, J3/J5 · high confidence in UI/source mismatch.**

The Chat model picker labels its first category Popular. Its caller ranks by at most 100 workspace request records and otherwise uses a fixed familiar-family ordering, including when history is absent or loading fails. The picker always labels its first eight usable models Popular; it receives no basis/availability indicator. Evidence: E17; `apps/dashboard/src/app/useModelPopularity.ts`, `features/playground/page.tsx`, and `features/playground/components/PlaygroundView.tsx`.

The finding is not that the ranking is completely fabricated or that defaults are undesirable. Recent workspace usage exists as one signal. The problem is undisclosed scope and fallback: an unmeasured default is presented with the same label as observed use.

Proposed direction: distinguish recent workspace usage from default suggestions and unavailable evidence. Do not invent global popularity or benchmark quality. Keep a useful picker when analytics is absent.

Verification: populated history, zero history and failed history retrieval produce honest category meaning. The scope/window are understandable where useful; a request failure must not make a default look like a measured recommendation.
title: UX-11: Popular implies stronger recommendation evidence than its fallback supplies

New API key → Limits & access policies shows Tokens/min as a numeric field without explaining its supported-request consequences. Proposed direction: keep creation concise and disclose the selected policy's material scope/consequences in context. Reuse the same semantics across creation, editing, summaries and downstream errors. Do not remove useful limits or require every user to read all advanced documentation.

The product implements explicit output capture into the workspace library, but the inspected dashboard offers no general retained-output inventory. Generations history does consume saved sessions and video tasks, so this is **not** a claim that task history is absent. Workspace Video → Materials instead requires a native Provider/key/model context and represents upstream materials. Evidence: E21, live navigation plus `SessionHistory.tsx`, `VideoResult.tsx`, `ImageReferences.tsx`, and the route registry. The shared Tasks/Assets integration is an intended capability in the generation handoff document.

Impact: “Save to workspace” has no matching workspace-library destination for browsing retained videos or managing retained copies independently of remembering the originating conversation. A source conversation can retrieve its retained video, which mitigates the problem; upstream Materials is not an equivalent destination. Current empty/expired data does not demonstrate that a particular user's saved bytes are lost.

Proposed direction: complete the retained-output discovery and management handoff with source-task context, ownership and availability. Decide its placement from the product blueprint; do not add a separate task system or merge upstream materials and retained outputs merely because both are files.

Verification: with authorized retained image and video records, leave the original conversation and locate the intended copy from the product's normal navigation, understand retention and access scope, return to the source, and find supported management actions. **P2 · visual meaning and content fidelity · G4, J5 · high confidence.**

An existing saved multi-turn Chat contains actual ordered lists. At 900 × 800 and 390 × 844, their items render as unnumbered indented lines. Read-only DOM inspection confirms `ol` elements with 51, 194 and 138 items, including a continued list with `start="195"`; both the list and its items compute to `list-style-type: none`. Evidence: E24; `styles.css` gives response lists indentation but no marker style. This is independent of whether the model fulfilled the requested item count.

Impact: readers cannot see sequence numbers or continuation numbering, refer to an item by number, or distinguish an ordered procedure from an unordered collection. Correct semantic elements alone did not preserve visual meaning. No screen-reader conformance result is claimed.

Proposed direction: style supported rich content as content, preserving ordered/unordered/nested markers and continuation values within the existing design system. Do not apply list markers indiscriminately to navigation or menu compositions.

Verification: inspect actual rendered ordered, continued, unordered and nested lists, alongside headings, quotations, code, tables and formulas when supported. Confirm visible meaning, narrow-width wrapping, and copy/export fidelity separately. [Tailwind Preflight](https://tailwindcss.com/docs/preflight#lists-are-unstyled) explicitly documents the reset; [W3C content structure](https://www.w3.org/WAI/tutorials/page-structure/content/) supplies the semantic distinction, not evidence of this particular rendering failure.

Source: docs/ux/findings.md (UX-17). Latest reconciliation: docs/ux/continuation-2026-10-21.md, All findings reconciled.

**P1 · commercial lifecycle completeness · G2/G5, J2/J6 · high confidence in implementation omission; populated commercial-media rendering untested.**

Provider administration supports media offers, but its Usage view renders only `data.consumption`, with input/output token columns. `crates/storage/src/provider_consumption.sql` restricts that collection to `billing_meter='text_tokens'`. The same backend summary separately returns `media_consumption` from non-text Provider earnings, with quantity, meter, dimensions, rates and unpaid amounts. `features/provider-business/admin.tsx` neither declares nor consumes that collection. Evidence: E28, live Usage surface and source contract/consumer comparison. Existing personal traffic is not evidence of missing payable charges.

Further consumer check (E33): the Provider member portal uses the same summary builder through `provider_member_dashboard`, which also returns `media_consumption`; `features/provider-business/page.tsx` declares and renders only text `consumption`. The current account can access the portal and its populated text offers, but current Usage is empty. This extends the omission to the Provider-facing investigation path without claiming an executed media-only dataset.

Impact: the operator's supported media business has no corresponding media-consumption detail in this Provider Usage page. A media-only earning history would still satisfy the UI's empty-text-collection condition for “No consumption in the last 90 days.” This conditional outcome is established by source, not an executed populated fixture. Other financial reports and API access may mitigate investigation; their presence does not make this page's broad claim accurate.

Proposed direction: carry supported billing variants through their investigation and reconciliation surfaces. Show media quantities and rate dimensions with their actual units, or explicitly narrow the text view and link to the relevant supported media evidence. Do not turn media quantities into tokens or expose procurement information in customer pages.

Verification: authorized media-only and mixed text/media commercial histories reconcile with Provider earnings and settlements; the detail explains quantity, agreed rate and unpaid amount. Empty-state wording describes the actual dataset. Confirm customer/Provider/operator visibility separately. No payable fixture or financial transaction was created in this audit.

description:
Source: docs/ux/findings.md (UX-18). Latest reconciliation: docs/ux/continuation-2026-10-21.md, All findings reconciled.

Imported disposition: Source-supported: finish reason is ignored; transport end becomes Complete. Saved partial/cancelled samples inspected, fresh upstream edge cases not executed

Recheck current code/rendering before implementing; migration is not a new reproduction or authorization for product changes.

**P2 · outcome status and recovery · G4/G5, J5/J6 · high confidence in parser behavior; no new upstream request or live rendered fixture.**

The current `runModel` function reads content and usage but not `finish_reason`; receiving the terminal stream marker leads to `phase: complete`. An isolated offline replay of the unchanged extracted parser with documented `stop`, `length` and `content_filter` cases returned `complete` and discarded the reason in every case. The empty-content cases also returned complete. The render branch labels that phase Complete, yet selects “Waiting for a response…” when content is empty and phase is not streaming/cancelled/failed. Evidence: E29, original parser/render source plus explicitly synthetic protocol fixtures. [OpenRouter's official API overview](https://github.com/OpenRouterTeam/docs/blob/main/api_reference/overview.mdx) documents distinct terminal reasons.

Impact: an output limit or filtered/empty terminal result cannot be distinguished from ordinary completion, and a terminal empty result is represented as still waiting. Users lack the information needed to choose a relevant remedy. The observed historical short lists do **not** establish why those specific requests stopped.

Proposed direction: retain and interpret supported finish reasons through live and saved results, separating transport termination, content outcome and unknown evidence. Explain a relevant next step without automatic paid retries or promises that increasing a limit will resolve every case.

Verification: cover ordinary stop, output limit with partial/empty content, filtered result, malformed response, missing terminal marker, cancellation and absent reason. Reopen persisted results. Offline parser tests establish mechanism only; rendered and genuine authorized request acceptance remain separate.
notes: Ten-outcome PostgreSQL real-router persistence/reopen acceptance passed (2.46s), 69 Chat integration tests passed. Evidence appended docs/ux/remediation.md. Added authorized streaming transport test for stop/length/content_filter against local synthetic HTTP upstream; combined chat_terminal_ run active handle 46961, log [local evidence path omitted]. No paid Provider execution. Keep open pending transport and rendered/live acceptance.
title: UX-18: Chat discards terminal reasons and conflates finished transport with complete content

Imported disposition: Active: unsupported default workspace pricing/enrollment; follow user-confirmed platform pricing direction

Recheck current code/rendering before implementing; migration is not a new reproduction or authorization for product changes.

**P1 · product model/complexity · G2, J2 · confirmed direction from user clarification; migration impact not yet assessed.**

Correction: the original recommendation to add a workspace standard-price enrollment path is withdrawn. It treated existing APIs and missing dashboard consumers as evidence that enrollment was a required user task. They establish implementation behavior, not product necessity.

Observation: Admin Pricing separates Standard prices and Workspace prices; the SDK exposes workspace enrollment methods. These observations (E02) remain valid. The product direction requires operator-managed selling prices, while workspaces organize access, usage attribution and limits. It does not establish a need for workspace-specific selling prices. The user clarified that the default should be platform-wide model pricing without per-workspace pricing or enrollment.

Impact: retaining this extra configuration layer makes operators manage price applicability separately for each workspace without an established customer need. Adding the missing enrollment UI would make that complexity more complete rather than resolve the product-model mismatch. The exact runtime and migration consequences still require implementation analysis.

Proposed direction: use platform-managed model selling prices as the default. Keep workspace permissions, limits and usage attribution distinct from pricing. Do not require a workspace tariff or price enrollment for ordinary authorized use. Customer contract prices or discounts require an explicit business requirement before introducing another pricing scope. Supply qualification and access checks remain necessary; publishing a price must not bypass either.

Verification: with qualified supply, an authorized customer can inspect the applicable platform price and use a model without workspace-specific pricing setup or enrollment. Requests retain the admitted price revision; later price changes do not reprice history. Verify text and media units, unavailable prices, denied access and unqualified supply separately. Before implementation, inventory existing overrides/enrollments and design an explicit compatibility/migration policy; this review does not authorize deleting contracts or records.

**P1 · consequential edit scope · G6, J7 · high confidence in draft behavior and save implementation; no policy submitted.**

In Model access, changing the unsaved model restriction to Block all enables Save. Navigating through Policy preserves the draft and shows a generic unsaved-changes notice, while the access card still says No restrictions from the saved policy. Opening External checks then shows an enabled Save despite no detector changes and no available detectors. That page provides no indication that a model restriction is pending. The shared `Guardrails` component submits the entire `draft` from every section's Save handler. Evidence: E30, actual unsaved navigation and screenshot, plus `features/guardrails/page.tsx` draft lifetime and PUT payload.

Impact: saving from an apparently unrelated section can also commit a hidden workspace-wide model block. The section title and local controls do not describe the effective submission scope. No actual block was enabled: Save was never clicked, and reloading cleared the test draft and disabled Save. The existence of one generic notice on the intermediate Policy page is mitigating evidence, but does not expose the pending changes at the commit point.

Proposed direction: make the commit boundary understandable. Either use explicitly section-scoped drafts and saves, or present a whole-policy editing model with a reviewable pending-change summary and discard path at its save point. Preserve atomic policy validation and revision conflict handling; do not assume separate API writes are required.

Verification: edit section A, visit B without editing it, and establish exactly which changes B's action would commit. Repeat with changes in both sections, invalid hidden input, cancellation, reload and conflict. Users can inspect and discard the affected changes before committing. Verify the saved outcome only with authorized isolated fixtures. [NN/g's usability heuristics](https://www.nngroup.com/articles/ten-usability-heuristics/) support visible state, error prevention and recognition at the point of action; they do not mandate a confirmation dialog for every save.
notes: GitHub #107: draft notice names every changed policy section, save applies all changes, discard clears draft; notice also accompanies History and Blocked requests. Restore is blocked with unsaved draft and reloads editor head after success. Shared policy regressions passed; cross-section rendered verification remains pending.

Proposed direction: identify the saved check and expose the processing information relevant to the decision. Distinguish historical binding from current configuration/availability; when details are no longer resolvable, say so rather than substituting present-day terms as historical fact. **P1 · state/recovery · isolated frontend probes + backend source.** A network rejection leaves an error and re-enables Create/Rotate without checking saved state or warning that the operation may have committed. After response loss, a create retry can create a second credential; a successful rotation may have already invalidated the old secret while the user never received the new one. Explain the uncertain credential state and direct the owner through explicit recovery. Preserve secret non-retrievability and prevent accidental duplicate issuance. Compare TopupFunding's existing uncertain-result handling rather than designing a generic retry loop.

**P1 · actor handoff · G3, J3 · high confidence in inspected entry points; end-to-end provisioning unverified.**

Observation: the account menu switches existing organizations; Organization settings creates workspaces; Users adds a person with a temporary access token; Account balances manages existing companies. None of these inspected entries exposes company creation or a provisioning guide. `docs/reference/company-creation.md` documents the administrator-only company-creation API. Impact: an operator onboarding a new independently funded customer must leave the dashboard and already know the company API. Creating another workspace in the current company is materially different because funds are shared.

Proposed direction: explicitly choose and document console-managed or API-managed company provisioning. Either needs a discoverable operator path through company, owner access, workspace, funds and first usable model. Do not add public self-signup or email invitations merely to imitate another product; those are separate product decisions.

Verification: a new operator can provision an independently funded customer using the supported path, hand off access and verify scope without using a developer's private instructions. Access creation, sign-in and isolation require separately authorized tests.
design: Console-managed customer provisioning is a separate task from Account balances. Reuse company, workspace, scoped owner and password APIs; no public signup or email invitations. Keep independent company funds and configured platform currency. Company, workspace and identity-only owner creation use atomic durable retry receipts. Identity creation issues no session; replay never restores changed/revoked access. Saved setup remains resumable, with tab retry caches disposable. Password configuration read and explicit revision-based reset support owner handoff. Do not label ready until sign-in, scope, supply/access/pricing and funding have been checked.

Source: docs/ux/findings.md (UX-04). Latest reconciliation: docs/ux/continuation-2026-10-21.md, All findings reconciled.

Imported disposition: Active, stronger evidence E02: absent global payment does not gate workspace features

Recheck current code/rendering before implementing; migration is not a new reproduction or authorization for product changes.

**P1 · global prerequisite gate · G3/G6, J3/J4/J8 · user-confirmed requirement; current absence observed.**

Observation: the inspected installation exposes workspace features while Settings → Payments reports online top-ups unavailable and payment gateways remain unconfigured (E05, E10). The earlier finding treated this as a local insufficient-funds recovery problem. The user clarified that valid payment setup is a hard global prerequisite: no workspace feature should become available before it is satisfied.

Impact: the product admits users into workspace workflows before a mandatory installation dependency is ready. Adding a funding link or a local warning would leave the global ordering failure intact. An existing balance, credit allowance or personal upstream key is not an implicit exemption from this setup gate.

Required direction: establish one server-authoritative installation payment-readiness gate shared by all workspaces. Until at least one supported payment method has valid, operational configuration, present an installation setup blocker instead of workspace features. Keep administrator payment setup, authentication, sign-out and necessary recovery/help accessible so the installation can be completed. Ordinary users see the blocker and its responsible operator, not merchant credentials or administration controls. Server-managed gateways may retain their supported configuration procedure; an in-dashboard editor is not inherently required.

Readiness must reflect the gateway's required credentials, merchant activation and required integration checks, not merely a saved configuration record. Apply the gate consistently to direct URLs, existing sessions and workspace API operations, not only navigation visibility. Preserve existing data and allow already-started payment callbacks, reconciliation and request settlement to complete. This gate is distinct from each customer's balance and from a single failed or pending payment; those do not by themselves make the whole installation unconfigured.

Verification: with no configured method, invalid/incomplete setup or unknown readiness, workspace entry and operations remain blocked across roles and entry points while an authorized operator can reach the remedy. Completing validated setup unlocks workspace access consistently. Removing or invalidating the last ready method re-establishes the gate without deleting records or abandoning in-flight obligations; another ready method keeps it satisfied. Verify pending/failed individual payments do not incorrectly block all users. Define operational readiness signals and temporary-outage handling before implementation; do not equate one failed transaction with global failure. Actual payment execution and migration remain separately authorized work.

description:

Impact: Migration 0432_api_key_secret_reveal.sql stores raw plaintext API key bearer tokens in api_keys.token_secret TEXT without application-layer AEAD encryption (unlike vendor credentials, OAuth tokens, payment keys, webhook secrets, and retained payloads which use CredentialCipher). Any DB backup, dump, or read replica in self-hosted/community or managed deployments exposes active spend-capable and delegated agent keys (pools:write, events:write, evaluations:write). Furthermore, token_secret is never purged when keys expire naturally (no cleanup in background_recovery.rs), GET /api/v1/workspaces/{workspace}/keys?reveal=true bulk-dumps all workspace secrets unlogged, and attach_key_secrets fetches every active workspace key secret even on single-key get_key.

description:

2. /catalog/v1/models (routes.rs:2336-2373), /api/v1/models (routes.rs:2500-2558), and /v1/models (routes.rs:1808-1841) return unpriced commercial models alongside sellable models with no callable/sellable gate or explicit unavailable state.

The detail panel (lines 505-533) displays 'Not published' with a generic disclaimer while still offering 'Open Generations', 'Create an API key', and a runnable curl example that leads users straight into HTTP 503.

title: Accept Stripe workspace funding for release 0.3

acceptance_criteria: Verify actual positive customer charge and balance/ledger conservation, explicit owner-funded/zero/unknown prices, usage and request inspection, exports and customer authorization. Provider expenses, procurement rates and margins must not leak into customer responses or UI. Verify nonzero credit configuration wording as well as the zero-price condition.
close_reason: Current customer billing and commercial boundaries verified against staging and independent artifacts.

description:
Trigger: user review of the global Settings dialog (2026-11-24). Chinese navigation and action labels are longer than necessary and repeat full phrases where a short noun or verb is unambiguous; e.g. 外观与语言, 成员管理, 额度与充值, 关于牛元, 显示名称, 保存更改, 修改密码, 版本发布说明, 反馈问题. The user also cited the call-to-action label 在对话中试用, which should be 试用.

Scope: settings dialog navigation, account/profile, password, appearance, organization, members header, billing labels owned by the settings surface, About, and the shared Try in Chat label.

Acceptance:
- Navigation reads 账户 / 外观 / 组织 / 成员 / 额度 / 关于.
- Buttons use short verbs (保存, 更换, 修改, 更新, 重试, 令牌加入) without losing meaning; labels use short nouns (名称, 语言, 余额, 订单, 明细, 发布说明, 反馈).
- Try in Chat renders 试用 (and its support-unverified variant 试用 · 支持未验证).
- No duplicated verbose subtitle where the same short meaning is already in the section title.
- English copy remains coherent; no functionality, routes, permissions, or persisted values change.
- Browser verify all six sections at 1440 and 390 in zh-CN, light/dark; build/tsc/i18n pass; regression coverage for the label contract.
notes:
Implemented and pushed as 52a2c93b on origin/release/0.4.

Labels:
- Settings navigation: 账户 / 外观 / 组织 / 成员 / 额度 / 关于.
- Account: 更换, PNG/JPEG/WebP · ≤ 5 MB, 名称, 保存, 用于登录此账户的密码。, 修改.
- Appearance: 颜色模式, 系统 / 浅色 / 深色, 语言, 仅用于此浏览器。, 保存中…, 重新加载.
- Organization: 新建组织, 常规, 名称, 标识, 新建工作空间, 加入组织, 令牌加入, 返回组织, 重命名, 访问令牌, 保存.
- Members: 成员, 管理成员、角色与工作空间权限。, 查看全部成员, 加载成员….
- Credits: 额度, 余额, 可用, 总额, 预留, 余额提醒, 关闭, 订单, 明细, 详情, 返回额度, 更多; simulated suffix 模拟.
- About: 开发版, 许可, 发布说明, 反馈, 文档（新标签页）, 第三方声明.
- Shared metadata/tabs: Members 成员, Credits 额度, Preferences 偏好, System 系统, Color mode 颜色模式, Language 语言.
- Model CTA remains the upstream concise 试用 / 试用对话 / 试用视频 contract; the new label test asserts it and rejects the old verbose keys.

Docs: Chinese settings navigation references updated in admin/customers, admin/payments, and getting-started. Concise-label invariant added to AGENTS.md and UI consistency standard.

Verification:
- Rebased onto upstream 377b7efa (which already unified the model trial CTA) and resolved locale-message overlap by keeping upstream Try/Try chat/Try video keys.
- Isolated worktree: LabelConsistency.test.ts 5/5 passed; pnpm build:dashboard passed (i18n, typegen, tsc, Vite build).
- Browser zh-CN: all six Settings sections at 1440 and phone width; nav/dropdown, account, appearance, organization, members, credits, About. Light and dark frames inspected. Models card exposes 试用. No horizontal overflow (docW = viewport at 390).

Local worktree note: another worker's uncommitted Empty-state changes remain in the shared worktree, so the local release/0.4 ref is still based on the pre-rebase commit; the verified label commit is on origin as 52a2c93b.
title: Simplify Chinese labels in the global Settings dialog

acceptance_criteria:
1. An ordinary authenticated user creates two distinct organizations with usable owner access and independent zero-funded billing; concurrent same-key retries return one result, changed input conflicts, uncertain-response recovery does not duplicate or silently grant funds. Onboarding clearly reaches an initial workspace and makes payment/supply prerequisites explicit.
2. One login can access multiple explicitly granted organizations. Authorized owners can add and manage members and their organization/workspace roles; invited/existing identities are linked only with a safe ownership/consent contract, not inferred from matching names or email. Test role changes, revocation, last owner, session expiry, sign-out/password reset and concurrent access changes; no workspace-only user can manage shared organization billing or grant organization access.
3. The user menu shows the current organization and can switch between actual authorized organizations. After switch, API/session authority, workspace selection, settings, usage and billing agree; direct links, reload, multiple tabs/sessions, empty organizations, failures and revoked memberships behave safely. Unauthorized organization identifiers and slugs never grant access. Verify desktop, intermediate and narrow layouts, opened menus, keyboard selection/focus/dismissal, loading/error/recovery and relevant sibling views.
4. Using at least two organizations with different members, workspaces, balances and rates, real backend/API integration tests demonstrate foreign reads/writes, exports and billing mutations fail, current authorized records succeed, and requests debit only the correct organization. Race tests cover switching/revocation against dispatch and transaction-time mutations; no procurement data appears in customer surfaces. Exercise self-funded internal-use behavior separately and preserve resale funding admission.
5. Upgrade tests migrate representative existing users, credentials, scoped roles, sessions, workspaces, Provider links, attempts, balances and invoices without unauthorized identity merging or changed historical attribution. Verify API/SDK/generated docs and legacy URLs; run relevant checks and rendered end-to-end flows. Record limitations/evidence and keep open until all acceptance criteria are met.

description:
Trigger and outcome: Niu currently models an operator session as belonging to one organization. An organization is the customer and shared billing boundary; it owns workspaces. A person needs one login for multiple independently funded organizations, each with separate members, access and billing. User confirmed that ordinary signed-in users can create multiple organizations and that the user menu should show the current organization and provide a low-prominence switcher.

Scope: Deliver the complete customer journey and agent/API contracts for self-service organization creation, organization identity and settings, organization and workspace membership administration, switching, and organization billing. A personal user may have their own organization; the organization, not each member individually, pays the Niu customer charges in resale mode. Internal-use provider funding remains separate. Organization owner/admin may manage shared billing within authorized scope; only the authorized member-management role may manage members. Workspace-scoped access must not become organization-wide authority. Platform administration and existing installation-only customer provisioning remain distinct.

Existing state and evidence: at source a1b9e0f41, admin_operators and sessions encode one organization and optional workspace; password credentials, profiles and revocation are attached to operators; account-menu selection changes client state and cannot expand session authority. Existing organization settings show identity and workspaces, and financial views are elsewhere. Existing platform customer provisioning niu-lxs.4 is not self-service organization creation. Partial local uncommitted work exists in crates/storage/migrations/0404_organization_identity.sql, crates/storage/src/account_organization_creation.rs, crates/storage/tests/account_organization_creation.rs, crates/storage/src/lib.rs and apps/dashboard/app/shell/AccountMenu.tsx. Treat it as provisional: inspect, revalidate, revise or replace as necessary. Migration 0404 and the storage creation method are not a complete identity system or public endpoint. Existing independent uncommitted dashboard changes must be preserved. niu-2n1 concurrently changes workspace navigation and proposes moving Members; coordinate against current work and keep organization-scope and workspace-scope permissions clear. niu-ayj.40 tracks broader member acceptance.

Design constraints: preserve existing users, sessions where safe, role grants, Provider ownership, workspace references, balances, request and invoice provenance across migration; never merge identities merely because names or email addresses look alike. Identity, organization memberships and selected session scope must be explicit. Creation must atomically establish ownership and independent zero-funded billing and recover safely from uncertain writes without duplicates; create a usable initial workspace or provide a clear supported setup flow. No customer-funded Provider execution may occur without the normal authorized price/funding admission. Changes of organization membership, role, session, password and revocation must be reflected at every authorization point, including transaction-time checks and concurrent operations. Do not broaden workspace members into organization admins or grant installation authority. Account/profile/password lifecycle must work across memberships without exposing or silently transferring another organization's data. Support loss of access, last-owner protection, concurrent changes and safe recovery. Do not invent an email-invitation delivery capability; make existing supported onboarding and its limitations explicit, or implement a complete authorized invitation flow if needed for the journey.

Switching: only show organizations the signed-in account is authorized to access; the server must resolve and authorize the selected membership, not trust a browser selection. The selected workspace, organization settings, usage, billing, requests and agent context must be scoped consistently. Handle no workspace, revoked access, stale tabs, multiple sessions, reload, direct URLs, failed/lost responses and in-flight requests without cross-organization disclosure or charging. Use durable readable organization slugs in browser paths/query scopes as required by AGENTS.md, while preserving existing API identifiers and authorized legacy routes/bookmarks; a slug is never authorization. Maintain customer-only financial serialization, prevent access to platform procurement and other organizations' balances, and retain historical accounting.

UI and documentation: use existing Niu shell and shadcn primitives. In the user menu show current organization and an accessible switcher without a prominent global header control; preserve selected-state checks and account actions. Make organization management discoverable with organization members, workspaces, settings and billing in the appropriate scope; do not label a workspace as an organization or expose internal IDs. Follow actual mature-product references, ux-review and the repo's browser verification gate, including open menu, keyboard, desktop/intermediate/narrow layouts and errors. Update affected English docs, agent onboarding, SDK/contracts and generated API documentation; mark limitations accurately. Keep niu.io as a resale deployment and maintain the separate self-hosted internal-use policy.
notes:
Handoff for agy: User requested requirements and Beads tracking only; do not interpret this handoff as authorization to change code in this turn. Work remains unfinished. Partial uncommitted storage implementation and a menu label change exist; review them before continuation. The isolated PostgreSQL test previously covered creation replay, changed input, separate identities, zero credit/entries, revoked target and revoked session; it did not validate HTTP, switching, member management, migration of real data, customer charges or financial isolation. Storage clippy and formatting passed. Preserve unrelated concurrent working-tree changes. Next: claim this task, reconcile navigation work with niu-2n1, inspect the partial code, and implement/verify the full acceptance criteria.
Completed and verified (2026-11-02):
1. Migration 0405_organization_slugs.sql adds durable organization slugs, organization_slug_aliases, immutable slug trigger, and backfills account_identities and account_memberships without merging identities by name/email.
2. Storage & Gateway: self-service POST /api/v1/organizations with optional slug and idempotency key, GET /api/v1/organizations/by-route/{route_slug}, PATCH /api/v1/organizations/{organization}, PUT /api/v1/session/organization, and POST /api/v1/session/memberships; account-level profile/preferences/password sync across linked memberships.
3. PostgreSQL integration tests: cargo test -p niu-storage --test account_organization_creation -- --ignored (3 passed, including migration_preserves_existing_identities_scopes_and_financial_attribution); cargo test -p niu-gateway --bin niu-gateway web::tests::passwords -- --ignored --test-threads=1 (7 passed, including multi-org isolation, financial debit isolation, internal-use mode, and switching/revocation races); customer_onboarding_provisions_shared_zero_credit_balance (1 passed).
4. Dashboard, SDK & Contracts: AccountMenu organization switcher & creation dialog, OrganizationSettings rename/slug/credits-prerequisite/embedded-Members/join-organization cards, OperatorCreateForm Scope DropdownMenu, SDK methods (renameCompany, switchSessionOrganization, claimSessionMembership), OpenAPI handler annotations (414 operations current).
5. Live browser verification on localhost:2566 across desktop (1440x900), intermediate (1024x768), and narrow (390x844) viewports, plus Vitest suites (54 + 40 tests passed) and zero-warning Clippy/tsc/hygiene checks.

description:

Impact: Even though the user is logged into the web dashboard, PlaygroundView.tsx:801-837,1125-1135,1252,1351-1367 and VideoView.tsx:223-239,448-454,485,493 require a workspace API key. Source: apps/dashboard/app/features/playground/components/PlaygroundView.tsx:801-837,979-987,1125-1135,1252,1351-1367; apps/dashboard/app/features/video/VideoView.tsx:223-239,448-454,485,493.

Chat now provides key creation and draft-preserving return without requiring a pasted secret, but still requires a workspace API key and Video is unchanged. This does not satisfy browser-session inference or automatic provisioning; issue remains open.
2026-11-04: Current inference admission and saved media lineage require a durable key ID; creating an unrestricted implicit key would evade existing key-specific spending, source IP, grant and rate policies and make revocation ambiguous. A complete session flow needs an explicit server-controlled authorization and policy model with atomic provisioning/dispatch checks, actor/workspace isolation, audit attribution and concurrency/revocation tests for Chat and Video. description: Trigger: app/lib/route-data.ts maintains a single activeRouteLoad and acquireRouteLoadSignal aborts it whenever authority/endpoint/path changes. React Router runs loaders for all matched routes in parallel; today loaders exist only on leaf routes, so the collision is latent. Adding a parent/child loader pair (the normal Data Mode pattern) would abort one of the two reads. Impact: future nested loaders fail intermittently with aborted requests; the current design cannot support nested data routes. Limits: not currently triggered because no route branch has two loaders.

description: Trigger: 15 route modules export loader() using loadCriticalRouteEndpoint (app/lib/route-data.ts:136+). On a cold cache it returns {status:'pending', promise} and swallows the promise rejection (void promise.catch), so the router never awaits data and errors never reach the route error boundary. Most pages call useOptionalRouteLoaderData() and ignore the result (customers/page.tsx:32, overview/page.tsx:24); only keys/page.tsx consumes it, and only when status==='ready'. Pages then fetch through useCachedQuery/useEffect, so loader data is unused on cold loads and duplicated on warm loads. Impact: Data Mode is nominal; loaders add latency/code without authoritative data, and loader errors are silent. Limits: no performance trace this pass.
title: P1: Route loaders are deferred snapshots that pages ignore or duplicate

description: Trigger: app/shell/AppLayout.tsx:1170 calls setActiveSessionSnapshot(...) during render, mutating a module-global (app/shell/router-context.ts:68). createRouterContextProvider reads that global, and React Router invokes getContext before each navigation's loaders. On the first load the global is empty, so loaders return unauthenticated/workspace-pending and are not revalidated when the session arrives (AppLayout only revalidates on mutation events, line 1184).
